findings.problem: fs::read_to_string performs file I/O directly inside a public function that should be pure data parsing; I/O leaks into what ought to be shell-only work
findings.failure_mode: domain logic cannot be unit-tested without real files; blocking I/O couples core parsing to filesystem availability; violates Data/Calculations/Actions split
findings.fix: Separate into: (1) fn parse_sensors(lines: impl Iterator<Item=&str>) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> (pure calculation) and (2) fn load_sensors(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> (shell I/O that delegates to parse_sensors)

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any file error (not found, permissions, encoding)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path or unavailable filesystem aborts the process instead of returning a typed error; violates panic freedom law
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use map_err to convert io::Error into a domain-typed error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric values in the second CSV field
findings.failure_mode: any malformed sensor reading crashes the process instead of returning a typed parse error; hostile input causes denial of service
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>; use map_err on parse to return a typed Invalid or Malformed error for non-u32 values

findings.problem: parts[1] uses unchecked indexing into the split result; panics if a line has only one comma-separated field
findings.failure_mode: short lines (missing second field) cause panic instead of returning a typed error; hostile or truncated input crashes the parser
findings.fix: Use parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) to return a typed error when the second field is missing

findings.problem: as u16 on a u32 parse result silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: sensor readings in range 65536-4294967295 wrap to incorrect lower values with no error; silent data corruption with no bounds check or overflow detection
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(value).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) to detect and reject out-of-range values with a typed error

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is logging (I/O) fused inside the data-parsing closure
findings.failure_mode: pure data logic has a side effect that cannot be suppressed for testing or embedded use; violates Functional Core / Imperative Shell; output appears even when no one requested it
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parser; if logging is needed, return parsed records and let the shell layer log after load_sensors returns

findings.problem: load_sensors fuses file I/O (line 9), string splitting (lines 12-15), logging (line 16), allocation (line 22), and domain construction (lines 17-20) into a single function
findings.failure_mode: no separation between Actions (I/O) and Calculations (parsing); pure logic cannot be tested without filesystem; all side effects are inseparable from core data transformation
findings.fix: Extract parse_sensors: &[str] -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> as pure calculation; load_sensors becomes a 3-line shell that reads the file, delegates to parse_sensors, and returns Result

findings.problem: Raw String values flow directly into Record without a parse boundary; no smart constructor validates the name field; the parse boundary is split instead of using split_once
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct invalid Record values directly with empty strings; split(',').collect() allocates for every field on every line and provides no field-count validation; parse boundary does not convert hostile primitives into trusted domain types
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) to get (_name, value_str) exactly once; add a smart constructor or validation on Record that rejects empty names; parse with split_once not split().collect()

findings.problem: Function returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures must panic via unwrap rather than returning typed errors
findings.failure_mode: no distinction between file-not-found, parse-invalid, overflow, and allocation failures; callers cannot handle specific error conditions gracefully
findings.fix: Define enum LoadError { Io(io::Error), Invalid, Overflow, TooMany } and fn load_sensors -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>; define enum ParseError { Invalid, Overflow } for the pure parser

findings.problem: Record stores name as String and value as u16 — both are raw primitives with no domain-level invariants encoded in the type
findings.failure_mode: illegal states are representable: empty name strings, zero values for required readings, any u16 including invalid ranges; no type-level enforcement of domain rules
findings.fix: Use newtypes like SensorName(String) with a smart constructor that rejects empty strings; add domain validation on value or use a typestate enum if value has lifecycle constraints

findings.problem: No benchmark evidence exists for the sensor-loading path; no baseline measurement for throughput or latency
findings.failure_mode: performance characteristics are unknown; allocation patterns from repeated split/collect on every line are unmeasured
findings.fix: Add criterion or similar benchmark measuring load_sensors across representative CSV sizes; measure allocations per record and total throughput

findings.problem: Every line allocates a Vec<String> via split(',').collect(), then clones strings into Record; no try_reserve or allocation budget
findings.failure_mode: unbounded per-line allocations degrade performance under large inputs; no allocation budget or bounded-capacity pattern is present
findings.fix: Use split_once to avoid intermediate Vec; pre-allocate the output Vec with try_reserve(record_count) where record count is known or estimated

findings.problem: No proof that cargo fmt, cargo check, cargo clippy, or cargo test commands were run; no CI gate evidence
findings.failure_mode: unknown if code compiles, passes lint gates, or has tests; delivery cannot be verified without command evidence
findings.fix: Run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy on strict settings, and cargo test; include exact commands and results in final response
